candidate_windows.window_text: For both tasks, we use the LoRA (Hu et al., 2021) method to fine-tune GLM-32k and Qwen-32k parameters efficiently. LoRA fine-tuning is a popular method to reduce the dependency on many training resources and yield high-quality results. We use $2^{*}\mathrm{A}6000$ GPUs for our experiments. For the EPR-S task, the model is trained for 15 epochs with the learning rate set as 1e-4 and the batch size as 48. For the EPR-T task, we use the same training epoch and learning rate. Due to the long context of around 30 dialogues, we set the batch size as 8. To obtain more stable predictions, we make the hyperparameter do_sample false to use greedy decoding at inference time.
